runs.interaction_thesis:
Tapping a slack row grows that row's own card into the full tide detail.
- The card's clip opens from the row's frame to the whole screen.
- The row's three lines (time, turn, next current) move to their places in the detail header, and the time scales up to the 56 pt hero.
- All of it runs on one `spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0)`, which never overshoots: slack water is the moment the current stands still.
- The rest of the detail fades in after the card has mostly grown (0.2 s ease-out, 0.15 s delay) and fades out first when closing (0.12 s ease-in).
- Dragging the header down collapses the card back into its row.

runs.interaction_thesis: Opening a slack from the Today list uses iOS 26's zoom navigation transition (`.matchedTransitionSource` on the row, `.navigationTransition(.zoom)` on the detail). The row grows into the tide detail as one surface and shrinks back into its own place on dismiss, including by dragging. Once the detail lands, the curve's slack marker settles in: the dashed rule draws top to bottom and the dot grows from 0.5 to 1. It runs on a critically damped `.spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0)` after a 0.35 s delay, because at slack the water stops and nothing in this app overshoots. With Reduce Motion on, the detail uses the system's automatic transition and the marker is already in place.
